data.one_liner: Flutter port of shadcn/ui offering customizable design system components.
data.what_it_does: Provides a comprehensive collection of UI components ported from shadcn/ui to Flutter. It includes common design system elements such as buttons, dialogs, forms, selects, context menus, and tooltips. The components are built to be highly customizable and serve as an alternative to default Material or Cupertino widgets.
use_when: Building web, desktop, or mobile applications that need a modern shadcn/ui aesthetic instead of default Material or Cupertino styles.
Requiring a cohesive design system with rich form controls, popovers, and overlay menus.
Creating multiplatform Flutter applications where desktop and web interactions like context menus and tooltips are central.
avoid_when: Your project strictly follows standard Material Design 3 or Apple Human Interface Guidelines.
You only need a single isolated widget and want to avoid adding a heavy suite of UI dependencies.
strengths: Extensive widget catalog including forms, popovers, context menus, sheets, calendars, and tables.
Comprehensive cross-platform support across mobile, web, and desktop.
Active development with frequent releases and bug fixes.
weaknesses: Pre-1.0 release with potential breaking changes between minor versions (e.g., dependency updates like slang).
Brings multiple transitive dependencies into your project (intl, slang, boxy, lucide_icons_flutter, etc.).

alternatives.name: material_ui
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick material_ui if you prefer standard Material-themed components rather than the shadcn design system.

alternatives.name: cupertino_ui
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick cupertino_ui if your application requires native iOS/macOS Cupertino-styled widgets.
